subject: The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
parts:
Hi all

How can i manage this warning? any help

mod <-'F1=~  q9+q10+q16+q17+q13+q20+q2+q4+q15+q5  
       F2=~  q8+q11+q14+q1+q12+q7+q19+q18
       F3=~  q6+q3'

baseline <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = mod, data = dat.tot1, ordered = names(dat.tot1), parameterization = "theta",
                          ID.fac = "std.lv", ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", group = "Country")

model.baseline  <- as.character(baseline)

fit.baseline <- cfa(model.baseline, data = dat.tot1, group = "Country", ordered = names(dat.tot1), estimator = "WLSMV")

Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue
    (= 2.472328e-17) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the
    model is not identified.

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
parts:
hear is  Terrence  answer
each with 7 categories (1 to 7)

Then the advice is pretty universal:  treat your indicators as continuous and use estimator = "MLR".  For example:

http://psychmodels.ucdavis.edu/uploads/8/6/3/9/86398102/rhemtullabrosseauliardsavalei_pm.pdf

When the estimator option is "WLSMV" or  " WLSM" below warning emerge and when it is  "DWLS" no warning. 

That is strange, since WLSM(V) is DWLS estimation with a robust chi-squared statistic and SEs.  Regardless, I'm guessing you won't see that warning if you treat your indicators as numeric (so 20 intercepts + 20 residual variances per country) rather than ordinal (120 thresholds per country).
